newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait stock volume hits record high despite Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait stock volume hits record high despite Iraq.

text.p: A strong display of U.S. military support for Kuwait helped push stock exchange traded value to a record high for the second week running during a continuing standoff with Iraq in the week to Wednesday, dealers said.

Other positive factors included progress by the government in repaying a $5.5 billion sovereign loan and steady repayments by Kuwaiti debtors involved in a programme to settle longstanding private sector obligations, dealers said.
"What is the worst that could happen -- he (Iraqi President Saddam Hussein) fires a missile? Even that would not affect the market," said Gulf Brokerage Company chairman Khaled al-Saleh.
"There is strong talk that a strike against Iraq will take place in 48 hours," one dealer whispered to a colleague. "Why should we care?" was the nonchalant reply.
Traded value rose to a record 233 million dinars ($779 million), a 12.5 rise from last week's previous record of 207.2 million dinars and equivalent to 46.6 million dinars a day.
The share index eased 4.4 points or 0.26 percent to 1,667.4 from last week's record 1,671.8.
"This little fall is normal after big increases over the past few weeks. It is profit-taking," said private dealer Mohammad al-Duhaishi.

Volume as measured by the number of shares traded over the week slipped to 1.021 billion shares from last week's record high 1.05 billion. Trade opens for two-and-a-half hours every day from Saturday to Wednesday.
The number of contracts executed rose five percent to an average of 2,232 a day. Losses led gains 23-17, with eight stocks unchanged.
Dealers said they were monitoring the situation with Iraq but felt no particular anxiety in view of the American support.

Washington dispatched eight Stealth warplanes and Scud- busting Patriot missiles to the Gulf Arab state and will send 3,500 more round troops in the next few days to help Kuwait confront what Washington calls direct threats from Baghdad.
The most active stocks were Commercial Bank, Investment Projects, Coast Development, United Realty, Pearl of Kuwait Real Estate and Kuwait Real Estate.
Banks were the most active sector by value with 43.2 percent, followed by investment shares with 24.2 percent and property companies with 23.8 percent.
Investments were the most active by volume with 33.4 percent. Banks came second with 31.3 percent and property firms third with 29.2 percent.
